residency.test: Resident if you intend to stay - 30 days with gainful activity, or 90 days without. Registering at the commune is decisive in practice.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for residents, but foreign real estate and permanent establishments are exempt with progression.
residency.note: Tax is levied at three levels: federal, cantonal and communal. The canton and even the commune you live in can change the bill by a factor of two.

headline.cantonal_communal: roughly 5% to 30% combined depending on canton and commune
headline.wealth_tax: cantonal wealth tax applies to worldwide net assets, typically 0.1% to 1%
headline.capital_gains: private capital gains on movable assets are tax free

employee.note: age-banded from 7% to 18% of the coordinated salary; plan-specific

capital_gains.movable_assets: private capital gains on shares and other movable assets are exempt from income tax
capital_gains.real_estate: cantonal real estate gains tax (Grundstückgewinnsteuer), heavily reduced for long holding periods
capital_gains.professional_trader: if the authorities classify you as a professional securities dealer, gains become taxable income and social security is charged on them

quirks: Where you live inside a canton matters. Communal multipliers mean two people with identical income a few kilometres apart can pay meaningfully different tax.

Foreign nationals without a C permit are usually taxed at source (Quellensteuer) through payroll. A full return is required above roughly 120,000 of income, and can be requested below that if deductions would help.
Private capital gains on securities are tax free, which is unusual and a major reason Switzerland scores well for investors - but wealth tax applies to the assets themselves every year.
Voluntary purchases into the second pillar (pension buy-in) are fully deductible and are the single largest planning lever for most employees.
Tax is assessed and paid by canton; moving cantons mid-year means your tax residence for the whole year is generally where you lived on 31 December.

reporting.authority: Cantonal tax administration, plus the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC)
reporting.portal: Each canton runs its own filing software and portal
reporting.who_must_file: Swiss citizens and C-permit holders always file. Source-taxed employees file if income exceeds roughly 120,000, if they have other income or assets above cantonal thresholds, or if they request an ordinary assessment.

deadlines.note: varies by canton - Zurich is 31 March, Geneva 31 March, Vaud 15 March

deadlines.what: Extensions are routinely granted, often to September or November, usually free or for a small fee
Deadline to request a subsequent ordinary assessment if taxed at source
Most cantons invoice provisional instalments during the year

forms.name: Cantonal return covering federal, cantonal and communal tax together
Salary certificate from the employer - the central document
Schedule of securities and bank accounts

documents_to_collect: Year-end bank statements for every account, including foreign accounts
Pillar 2 and pillar 3a contribution certificates - both are deductible
Mortgage interest statement and the tax value of any property
Receipts for professional expenses, commuting and further education

penalties.late_filing: reminder, then an ex officio assessment based on estimated income, plus a fine
penalties.evasion: typically the evaded tax plus a penalty of the same amount again; voluntary disclosure is penalty-free once in a lifetime

warnings: Cantonal and communal rates here are single approximate effective rates. Real cantonal schedules are progressive and commune-specific - always confirm with the official cantonal calculator before relying on a number.
Wealth tax is not modelled and can be significant for asset-rich taxpayers.
The federal married scale is approximated by an income-splitting factor rather than the true separate table.
